text: The simplest two-step cipher swaps each letter for another by a fixed table, then moves the letters around. Experiment 19 tried about 24,000 moves; since then the project has built them by the million.
For each move, the same known letter must always land on the same carved letter, and two different known letters never on the same one. E alone, three times among the cribs, is a strong test.
1,835,741 moves in four sets: not one admits a swap table, on K4 or on any of ten scrambled coppers.
